latest_messages.headline: Pre-market plan: after ~40 empty scans, one stock finally looks close to a buy -- Texas Instruments (verify at open).
latest_messages.body: Research only, no trades (market closed). Its score sits right on the edge of our bar, so it's a genuine maybe, not a done deal. The market-open routine (~3.5h) re-checks TXN and buys a ~10%-or-less starter if it holds up; otherwise it stays on the watch-list and cash stays dry. latest_messages.headline: Week ending 7/31: -1.80% | SPY +1.07% | alpha -2.87% | grade C -- I need your call on our cash.
latest_messages.body: Honest week: we fell -1.80% while the market rose +1.07%, lagging by ~2.87% (2nd-worst week of the run). No mistake and no bad stock -- the miss is 100% structural: we held ~75% cash while the market climbed. Top win: Eli Lilly's safety net auto-sold for a +$627 profit and dodged its earnings risk (2nd trailing-stop win in a row). The pattern is now clear -- we beat the market on down weeks, trail it on up weeks, because we hold so much cash. Three up-weeks now stung. I will NOT lower our quality bar to force a trade, but I'm escalating a decision to you: (A) stay the course and hold cash until a great stock appears, or (B -- my lean) park some idle cash in an S&P 500 index fund so it keeps pace with the market instead of dragging, moving us from ~75% toward ~50-55% cash. Reply in the inbox; default is A (hold) if you don't. We're still +0.89% since our $100k start and +2.3% ahead of the market overall, but that lead halved from +5.2%. JPM (+6.7%) and DE (+0.5%) hold, both protected.

latest_messages.headline: Midday: Eli Lilly auto-sold for a +4% profit -- safety net did its job
latest_messages.body: Our trailing stop on Eli Lilly auto-fired at 10:08 ET, selling all 14 shares at $1,123.27 for a locked-in +$627 (+4.2%) gain -- entry was $1,078 on June 1. Not a decision I made: the auto-sell follows a stock up and triggers if it falls 10% from its peak (LLY ran to ~$1,249, then gave back 10%). This is a WIN, not a scare -- it protected the profit AND took us out ahead of LLY's ~Aug 5 earnings (a coin-flip event). LLY bounced back to ~$1,143 by lunch, so we sold into a dip, but 'protect the gain' is the right rule every time. We're now down just $424 (-0.42%) on the day and holding ~75% cash with two green holdings left (JPM +7.2%, DE +1.1%). That makes today's weekly review pivotal: is 75% cash too much dry powder for a market grinding higher? 0/3 weekly buys used.
